About

The short version

I started in architectural design and drifted toward the part of the job everyone else treated as a deliverable: the moment a client finally sees the building.

Fourteen years later that moment is my whole job. At MG2 I run the Visualization Technology department solo, which means I’m the strategy, the pipeline, and the person hitting render. 3D rendering, film cinematics and editing, VR/AR/XR, interactive experiences: if it helps someone understand a design before it exists, it comes through my desk.

Coming from the design side means I read drawings, sit comfortably in design crits, and know which details sell a space. The work reads as architecture, not just imagery.

2005–12
Architecture school, twice over — B.Des at Florida (high honors), M.Arch at UVA. Learned to draw by hand and never really stopped: watercolor, charcoal, physical models.
2013–14
Freelance 3D artist. Renderings and real-time assets in early Unreal and Unity, built from whatever clients had: sketches, CAD files, sometimes just a phone call.
2014–18
Illustrate My Design. Started as a 3D artist, ended up managing a team of five across 100+ architecture and interiors projects.
2018–22
MG2, architectural designer. Project Architect on retail, food & beverage, and grocery work — Revit, code, permitting, construction admin. The years that make my renders read like buildings instead of backdrops.
2022–now
MG2, Design Visualization Specialist. Built the firm’s end-to-end viz pipeline from scratch; art direction and QA standards across 100+ projects a year; training curricula for 300+ designers; a fleet of 15+ VR headsets across six offices.

The formal version lives in the resume (PDF).
